To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neural network estimates of the rms error profiles of individual infrared or microwave atmospheric temperature and moisture profiles are accurate to about 10 percent of the dynamic ranges of the profiles, and that these estimates can be used to improve the weighting of soundings during assimilation.

(a) neural network estimation of retrieval variances is possible for individual profiles, and (b) the estimated variances can be stratified to provide more accurate weighting of soundings in assimilation.

neural networks can be developed to accurately estimate the rms errors in individual infrared and microwave sounding profile retrieval accuracies, thus significantly improving the ability to weight individual profiles in the assimilation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing and testing neural network algorithms for estimating the rms error of individual atmospheric temperature and humidity profiles retrieved by hyperspectral infrared and hyperspectral microwave sounders.
improving the assimilation of satellite soundings by estimating the variance of individual soundings and using this information to improve the weighting of soundings against model variables.
the development of new techniques for estimating the accuracy of individual profiles, which is a key component of data assimilation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the neural network approach for estimating retrieval variances has the potential to significantly improve the assimilation of hyperspectral infrared or microwave soundings into numerical weather prediction.
the neural network approach for estimating the rms error of individual retrievals has the potential to greatly improve the assimilation of infrared and microwave soundings. [1]
the new neural network variance estimates are very useful for improving the assimilation of infrared and microwave sounding observations into NWP models. [1]

neural networks are a very powerful tool for estimating the accuracy of atmospheric profile retrievals from satellite observations.
we have shown that neural network estimates of the accuracy of individual profiles from infrared and microwave hyperspectral sounders are feasible.
we are developing the tools to enable the full exploitation of the potential for accurate retrieval of atmospheric profiles from infrared and microwave hyperspectral measurements.

hyperspectral soundings have great potential for providing accurate estimates of individual sounding variances, thus potentially improving the assimilation of soundings into weather models.
